requested: Execute the accepted repository simplification in one offline transaction
preserved: Algorithm, reward, tensor, checkpoint, backend and target-domain behavior except for the new explicitly clean baseline profile
forbidden: Branch creation, training, simulation, commit, push, checkpoint rewrite or method redesign

review.scope: Plan ownership, topology, removal and research-ML boundary review

source_edits.scope: Complete local repository refactor without branch creation or live work
source_edits.receipt: User explicitly requested one-shot execution on 2026-09-07

dimensions.name: responsibility-ownership
dimensions.evidence: Hydra leaf profiles own experiment values, training application owns lifecycle, and FADA stage namespaces own public method entry surfaces.

dimensions.name: public-interface
dimensions.evidence: The existing train script remains the CLI while implementation helpers move behind unilab.training.offpolicy; checkpoint metadata remains authoritative.

dimensions.name: dependency-direction
dimensions.evidence: Scripts depend on training and method packages; no environment or backend dependency is inverted toward scripts or FADA workflows.

dimensions.name: state-lifecycle
dimensions.evidence: Tracker start/update/finish and runner close stay in one application owner; checkpoint state and schemas are unchanged.

dimensions.name: change-surface
dimensions.evidence: Characterization tests precede canonical config replacement, entrypoint extraction and public namespace migration; context calibration remains out of scope.

dimensions.name: evidence-boundary
dimensions.evidence: Offline composition and unit tests establish structure and preserved behavior only; training and policy quality are not claimed.

dimensions.name: proof-route
dimensions.evidence: RED tests cover canonical profile semantics, inheritance depth, retired selectors, thin script ownership and stage imports; focused and full tests close GREEN.

dimensions.name: architecture-topology
dimensions.evidence: The plan removes lifecycle implementation from the script and reduces command callers from flat implementation modules to stage APIs.

dimensions.name: ownership-convergence
dimensions.evidence: Experiment values cease to be accumulated across several historical YAML owners; canonical leaf files become the only active owners.

dimensions.name: caller-knowledge
dimensions.evidence: Callers select one canonical task or one FADA stage API and no longer know intermediate experiment history.

dimensions.name: tensor-provenance
dimensions.evidence: No observation projection, tensor shape, dtype, device, mask or privilege consumer is changed.

dimensions.name: gradient-update-boundary
dimensions.evidence: Learners, losses, optimizers and update counts remain unchanged.

dimensions.name: persistence-evaluation
dimensions.evidence: Checkpoint schemas remain unchanged and canonical profile mapping is documented; mismatched metadata continues to fail before mutable setup.

dimensions.name: removal-reachability
dimensions.evidence: Repository consumers are migrated and searched before old task YAML and launchers are removed; historical documents are retained as evidence.

lifecycle_owners: scripts/train_offpolicy.py owns tracker, runner and playback lifecycle
unilab.training.offpolicy owns tracker, runner and playback lifecycle

removed_dependency_edges: experiment task -> preceding historical experiment task
reduced_caller_knowledge: command scripts no longer import flat stage implementation modules
consolidated_lifecycle_owners: off-policy lifecycle is owned in the training package instead of the CLI script
clarified_semantic_owners: one canonical leaf owns each active experiment identity

file_metrics.before: 25 G1 SAC task YAML and 796-line off-policy script
file_metrics.after: 11 G1 SAC task YAML and 48-line CLI with application/factory/playback owners

architecture_delta.rationale: The change removes historical configuration dependencies and moves lifecycle ownership behind the existing training package boundary.

residual_risks: External commands using retired historical task names must migrate using the documented mapping.
No simulator or training evidence is authorized, so policy quality remains unknown.
